rule: Carb tier by session type: high = lower, full_body, run_long, run_quality, hyrox, metcon, test, competition, race (and the day before a long run/race); moderate = upper, sprint_upper, run_easy; low = recovery, rest
summary: 'Fuel for the work required' and the consensus statements support raising carbohydrate on days with a high glycogen cost (long and quality runs, Hyrox, metcons, races, the day before a long run) and lowering it on rest and recovery days. That idea is well supported, but the mapping of each session type is a coaching judgement. The weakest placement is 'lower' (heavy strength) in high: strength-training reviews find little or no carbohydrate dose-response for resistance performance, and resistance work rarely depletes glycogen. Because tiers only redistribute a fixed weekly total, the cost of a misplacement is small. If MacroFactor's total gets tight, 'lower' is the first candidate to move to moderate so run_long, run_quality and Hyrox days keep their carbs.

sources.note: Impey 2018: adjust carbohydrate to the demands of the upcoming session; glycogen threshold hypothesis
Burke 2011: high carbohydrate availability for high-intensity or key sessions; train-low benefit for performance unclear
Henselmans 2022: no carbohydrate dose-response for strength performance; benefit mainly in high-volume (>10 sets/muscle) sessions
Escobar 2016: 3-7 g/kg for resistance training may be more than needed; true glycogen depletion unlikely
